canonical_data: Git-versioned Markdown brain repositories, with PGLite or Postgres retrieval projections, typed links, citations, and durable background-job state
current_repo_note: The Git repository is the canonical project and install source; the unrelated npm package named gbrain is not this system.
strengths: Git-versioned Markdown remains the system of record while PGLite or Postgres provides hybrid lexical, vector, and graph retrieval
Synthesis, citations, gap analysis, contradiction checks, consolidation jobs, and durable agent-facing memory operations go beyond raw chunk search
Local CLI, stdio and HTTP MCP, broad model and embedding providers, and self-hosted deployment preserve strong portability
weaknesses: The very broad CLI, server, graph, job, skill, evaluation, and integration surface creates meaningful setup and upgrade complexity
Semantic retrieval, extraction, synthesis, and some ingestion paths depend on optional external model or SaaS providers
The project is young and changing quickly despite strong adoption, extensive tests, and unusually detailed operational documentation
Some enrichment paths need paid model services, and durable subagent loops remain Anthropic-specific
why_it_matters: Combines human-owned, Git-versioned memory with production-oriented retrieval, graph, synthesis, provenance, and agent integration in one local-first system.
